title: Quantization x Steering Fragility: Does Compressing a Model Break Its Safety Steering Vector?

original_idea.body: A safety steering vector validated on fp16 may lose effect or flip sign on int8/int4 quantized models people actually deploy; measure effect retention.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quantized deployment is the norm; showing safety steering doesn't survive it has a clear defensible chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Extract vector, apply to int8/int4 via bitsandbytes, measure retention; standard tools, beginner-friendly.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single experiment: same vector across quantization levels, measure retention/sign flips.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Consumer/edge quantized deployment is exactly the open-community slice labs deprioritize; no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Quantized models reduce memory; inference-only, easily single consumer GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Quantization x steering-fragility interaction appears largely unexplored.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The quantization-induced drift of safety steering vectors is a practical interaction with no direct published work known.
